headline: Highest risk is data leakage: kotaemon’s broad network/API and secret-handling can expose dagster-orchestrated data if paired without isolation; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP surfaces, so direct injection into it is not documented. Kotaemon is a web UI RAG app that can ingest documents and chat transcripts, so if operators manually pass its outputs into Dagster configs or tasks, prompt content could influence downstream behavior. The bridge is manual and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies kotaemon-generated text into Dagster job definitions or run parameters
IF Dagster is configured to parse user-provided text as instructions
mitigations: Keep a human review step before any Dagster execution
Use a fixed template for Dagster parameters
Strip instruction-like text from kotaemon outputs before reuse
Separate chat/RAG outputs from orchestration inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no network egress, but kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can call third-party APIs by default. If both share a workspace or files are moved from kotaemon into Dagster-managed pipelines, sensitive content can flow into external inference services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default kotaemon deployments.
conditions: IF kotaemon is configured to use OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Groq, or similar external APIs
IF files from kotaemon's ./ktem_app_data or uploaded documents are shared into Dagster workflows
mitigations: Disable external LLM providers in kotaemon
Store kotaemon data on a separate volume from Dagster
Block secrets from being uploaded into RAG sources
Review API egress settings before enabling shared pipelines
Use redaction on documents before ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or egress network, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with kotaemon in the usual sense. Kotaemon can use files and multiple instances, but the pair lacks overlapping write authority to the same mutable target in the profiles. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator mounts the same writable directory into both agents
IF additional write-capable plugins are added to Dagster or kotaemon
mitigations: Mount separate working directories
Run each agent under distinct OS users
Avoid shared git repositories for both tools
Add file-locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster does not verify or consume kotaemon outputs by default, but a common workflow is to use kotaemon to summarize documents and then feed those summaries into downstream automation. Because kotaemon can emit citations and extracted text while Dagster can orchestrate pipelines, an unverified handoff could propagate errors into scheduled work products. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF kotaemon summaries are copied into Dagster pipeline inputs without review
IF Dagster automates actions based on kotaemon-generated citations or extracted facts
mitigations: Require manual verification of kotaemon outputs
Add schema checks before Dagster consumes text
Log source provenance alongside summaries
Use a second reviewer for high-impact pipelines

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon handles API keys and can send document contents to third-party APIs, creating residency and retention concerns; Dagster itself shows no sensitive data classes or egress. The compliance risk is therefore concentrated in kotaemon, but the pair can still breach policy if Dagster workflows move regulated documents into kotaemon-backed external services. Dagster is not cited for the specific violation because its profile shows no such handling.
conditions: IF regulated documents are ingested into kotaemon while external API providers remain enabled
IF retention or residency rules prohibit sending those documents to third-party inference services
mitigations: Use local-only models in kotaemon
Disable or restrict external API providers
Classify and block regulated documents at ingestion
Document retention and deletion settings
Keep Dagster workflows outside regulated-data paths
